name: Residual volatility to BTC (90-day OLS), top half by residual vol sized by inverse realised volatility, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. For every symbol with L >= need: r_s[k] = ret(b_s,k), k = e-window+1..e; x = the same series for BTCUSDT (if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew). OLS with intercept of r_s on x: beta_s = cov(r_s,x)/var(x), alpha_s = mean(r_s) - beta_s*mean(x); residual_k = r_s[k] - alpha_s - beta_s*x_k; ivol_s = sample standard deviation of the residuals (BTCUSDT: ivol = 0 by construction, it is scored and never selected). n = scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Sort descending by ivol; H = the floor(selectFrac*n) highest-ivol symbols. sigma_s = sample standard deviation of r_s over the same window (total, not residual, as c1023-r2-03). w_s = (1/sigma_s) / sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: A coin with low correlation to BTC is exactly a coin whose variance is mostly residual to BTC, so c1023-acad2-25 (high idiosyncratic vol, weekly, EW-market regressor) and c1023-r2-03 (low correlation, inverse-vol) may be one factor seen through two sorts; this spec uses r2-03's cadence, window, half-selection and sizing with acad2-25's residual-volatility sort against BTC, so the three numbers can be read together.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 1; extends c1023-acad2-25 and c1023-r2-03; Zhang & Li 2020 Physica A 553 (crypto idiosyncratic volatility); Ang, Hodrick, Xing & Zhang 2006 JF

name: Low BTC-correlation sleeve, bottom half, 70th-percentile hold buffer, sized by inverse realised volatility, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank ascending by corr; percentile p_s = (position-1)/(n-1). Hold set H in ctx.state (starts empty; ctx.state.H === undefined -> []): drop s from H if it is unscored or p_s > holdPct; then add symbols in ascending corr order (skipping ones already in H) until |H| = ceil(selectPct*n) (exactly c1023-r2-05's buffer). sigma_s = sample standard deviation of ret(b_s,k) over k = e-window+1..e. w_s = (1/sigma_s) / sum over H of (1/sigma); weights sum to 1. If n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need: reset H to empty and return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The two single changes to the correlation sleeve that survived round 2 were the hold buffer (r2-05, less turnover) and inverse-vol sizing (r2-03, equal risk per pick); applying both at once asks whether they stack or were the same improvement.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 2; extends c1023-r2-05 and c1023-r2-03; Novy-Marx & Velikov 2016 RFS (buffer rules); Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen 2012 FAJ (risk parity)

name: Core-satellite: 50% BTC fixed plus 50% in the rank-weighted low-BTC-correlation sleeve, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. Rank weights (c1022-redteam-04): sort descending by corr (position 1 = highest corr); weight of position q = q/T with T = n(n+1)/2, so the lowest-correlation name gets the largest weight. Sleeve weights v_s are those rank weights (sum 1, BTCUSDT at position 1 with the smallest weight). Final w_s = (1-core)*v_s for every scored s, plus core added to BTCUSDT (w_BTC = core + (1-core)*v_BTC). Weights sum to 1. If n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need return ew. Monthly, long-only. Reference for the report (not a ledger id): the same bars held as {BTCUSDT: 1}, so the question 'does the sleeve add to a BTC holder' is read from this id versus BTC-only, beside the harness's EW benchmark.
rationale: c1023-r2-02 showed that holding only BTC in the 'wrong' regime loses, so the practical question for a BTC holder is whether a half-position in the low-correlation sleeve improves on BTC alone rather than on an equal-weight alt book; a fixed 50/50 core-satellite is the simplest version of that question.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 4; extends c1022-redteam-04 and c1023-r2-02; Frazzini & Pedersen 2014 JFE; Amenc, Malaise & Martellini 2004 JPM (core-satellite)

name: Low-BTC-correlation picks sized proportional to (1 - correlation), monthly (continuous tilt)
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. corr_s = Pearson correlation of ret(b_s,k) and ret(b_BTC,k) over k = e-window+1..e (BTCUSDT gets corr = 1); a symbol with L < need is skipped; if BTCUSDT has L < need return ew; n = number of scored symbols; if n < minNames return ew. raw_s = max(0, 1 - corr_s) for every scored symbol (BTCUSDT: raw = 0; corr lies in [-1,1] so raw lies in [0,2]). Z = sum of raw over scored symbols; if Z <= 0 return ew. w_s = raw_s / Z; weights sum to 1. If n < minNames or BTCUSDT has L < need return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The rank weights of redteam-04 throw away the size of the correlation gap; a weight proportional to 1 - corr is the continuous version of the same tilt and tells whether the signal is ordinal only or carries information in its magnitude.

name: r2-09 leg (a): two-week momentum top 4 in greed, cash in fear, equal weight when neutral or unavailable, weekly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. g = ctx.macro('FNG') (null before 2018-02). eligible = symbols with L >= lookback+1, score_s = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1. If g is not null and g >= greed: hold the top `top` by score, 1/top each (if fewer than top eligible, 1/|eligible| each). If g is not null and g <= fear: return {} (cash). Otherwise (neutral or null): equal weight over eligible. Weekly, long-only. The greed and neutral legs are byte-for-byte c1023-r2-09's; only the fear leg changes (sleeve -> cash).
rationale: c1023-r2-09 combined a greed-momentum leg with a fear low-correlation leg; this spec keeps the momentum leg and replaces the fear leg by cash so the combined number can be attributed to its parts without touching the combined spec.

name: High downside beta, sleeve volatility matched to the EW universe with the residual in cash, exposure check (e) as a hard gate (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Downside beta (r25-downside-beta-high construction): elig = symbols with L >= need; M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew; market m_j = mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..window-1; down = {j: m_j < 0}; if |down| < minDown return ew; md = mean of m over down, var = sum over down of (m_j-md)^2 (if var <= 0 return ew); beta_s = sum over down of (r_s,j - rd_s)(m_j - md) / var with rd_s = mean of r_s over down (same centring as the parent module). N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)); sleeve = the N highest beta_s. sigma_S = sample std over j = 0..volWindow-1 of (mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j)); sigma_M = same for elig; w = sigma_S > 0 ? min(1, sigma_M/sigma_S) : 1. Weights: w/N on each sleeve name, nothing else (the residual 1-w is cash, not the equal-weight universe as in c1023-r2-19). Monthly, long-only. Gate (declared now, applied at retest, same wording as c1023-r2-19): this id counts as ahead only if the retest exposure check (e) passes (strategy CAGR > exposure x B&H CAGR and strategy Sharpe > B&H Sharpe); a check-(e) fail is a FAIL for this id regardless of excess.
rationale: c1023-r2-19 passed every retest leg except the exposure check (e), and its residual sat in the equal-weight universe, which is the benchmark itself; putting the residual in cash means the book can only be ahead by picking better names, not by holding more risk than the benchmark.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 8; extends c1023-r2-19 and r25-downside-beta-high; Ang, Chen & Xing 2006 RFS; Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015 JFE

name: Lower-tail dependence with the market sorted inside the high-volatility half (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. Panel (c1023-acad2-03 construction, unchanged): eligible = symbols with L > 505; daily returns keyed by calendar day over the last window+1 bars; cal = the last `window` union days; market m_d = mean over eligible names with a return on day d; names = eligible symbols with a return on every day of cal; if |cal| < window return {}. q_m = 5th percentile of m (linear interpolation); tail = {d: m_d <= q_m}; if tail is empty return {}. LTD_s = (# d in tail with r_s,d <= q_s) / |tail| with q_s = 5th percentile of r_s over cal. New cut (c1022-acad-61's): vol_s = sample std of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..volBars-1, on names; HV = the floor(highVolFrac*|names|) highest-vol names. k = floor(topFrac*|names|) (20% of the full count, as c1023-r2-21); if k < 3 return {}; hold the k highest LTD_s within HV, 1/k each. Parameters window, tailPct and topFrac are acad2-03's untouched; this is a new universe cut, not a retune.
rationale: acad2-03 was the strongest round-2 academic sort (forward-positive, beat the control, failed only its -25% neighbour by 0.3pp); acad-61 showed the high-volatility half sharpens a cross-sectional sort, so the crash-sensitivity premium should be easier to see among the names where crash exposure is largest.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 12; extends c1023-acad2-03 and c1022-acad-61; Chabi-Yo, Ruenzi & Weigert 2018 JFQA; Bandarchuk & Hilscher 2013 JFM

name: 12-1 momentum among high-volatility, top-half dollar-volume names with the sleeve volatility-scaled to a 10% tracking target (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L > 260 (acad-61's guard); N = |elig|; if N < minNames return ew. dv_s = mean of close*volume over k = e-dvWindow+1..e; liquid = the ceil(N/2) highest dv (c1023-r2-16). vol_s = sample std of ret(b,e-m), m = 0..volBars-1, on liquid; HV = the floor(highVolFrac*|liquid|) highest-vol names within liquid. mom_s = b[e-skip].close/b[e-form].close-1 on HV; k = floor(topFrac*|liquid|) (so the sleeve is the same 40% of its high-vol pool as in acad-61 and c1023-r2-13); sleeve = the k highest mom_s (k < 3 -> return ew). Spread series s_j = mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j) - mean over elig of ret(b,e-j), j = 0..spreadWindow-1; sd = sample std of s * sqrt(252); w = sd > 0 ? min(1, target/sd) : 1. Weights: (1-w)/N on every elig name plus w/k on each sleeve name (c1023-r2-13's construction). Monthly, long-only.
rationale: The two single changes that survived round 2 on top of acad-61 were Barroso-Santa-Clara scaling of the sleeve (r2-13) and the top-half dollar-volume cut (r2-16); combining them tests whether the high-vol momentum edge holds once it is both risk-controlled and restricted to tradable names.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 13; extends c1022-acad-61, c1023-r2-13 and c1023-r2-16; Bandarchuk & Hilscher 2013 JFM; Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015 JFE; Korajczyk & Sadka 2004 JF

name: 12-1 momentum top 20% with the sleeve volatility matched to the EW universe, residual in cash, exposure check (e) as a hard gate (wide US stocks), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. elig = symbols with L >= need; M = |elig|; if M < minNames return ew. mom_s = b[e-skip].close/b[e-form].close-1; N = max(minHoldings, round(fraction*M)); sleeve = the N highest mom_s. sigma_S = sample std over j = 0..volWindow-1 of (mean over sleeve of ret(b,e-j)); sigma_M = same for elig; w = sigma_S > 0 ? min(1, sigma_M/sigma_S) : 1. Weights: w/N on each sleeve name, residual 1-w in cash (identical construction to c1024-r3-09 applied to the momentum sort). Monthly, long-only. Gate (declared now, applied at retest, same wording as c1023-r2-19): this id counts as ahead only if the retest exposure check (e) passes (strategy CAGR > exposure x B&H CAGR and strategy Sharpe > B&H Sharpe); a check-(e) fail is a FAIL for this id regardless of excess.
rationale: Clusters C and D are the two equity themes that were forward-positive in both rounds; giving 12-1 momentum the same vol-matched, cash-residual, gated construction as the downside-beta book (idea 8) makes the two clusters comparable on equal exposure terms.

name: 9-ETF dual momentum with the lookback decided by a 3/6/12-month majority vote (QQQ, DIA, GLD, DBC, VNQ vs AGG, IEF, TLT, SHY), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. R_h(s) = b[e].close/b[e-h].close-1 for a symbol in the view with L >= need (others unscored). For each horizon h in horizons, the horizon's verdict v_h is c1023-r2-24's rule at that lookback: bestRisk_h = scored risk symbol with the highest R_h (ties by name), bestSafe_h = scored safe symbol with the highest R_h; v_h = bestRisk_h if bestRisk_h exists and R_h(bestRisk_h) > 0 and (bestSafe_h is absent or R_h(bestRisk_h) > R_h(bestSafe_h)); else v_h = bestSafe_h if it exists; else v_h = null. Hold {s: 1} for the symbol s named by at least two of the three verdicts; if all three verdicts differ, hold v_tieHorizon (the 6-month verdict, fixed now); if that is null return ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: c1023-r2-24's excess fell from +7.1 to +3.0pp when its 12-month lookback was moved 25%, so the lookback is its fragile parameter; a majority vote over 3, 6 and 12 months is the standard way to stop one horizon's noise flipping the switch.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 15; extends c1023-r2-24; Antonacci 2014 'Dual Momentum Investing'; Faber 2010 'Relative Strength Strategies for Investing' (multi-horizon averaging); Keller & van Putten 2012 (FAA)

name: 9-ETF dual momentum with a 20% volatility-managed overlay on the risk holding, remainder in the best safe ETF, monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. R(s) = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1 for a symbol in the view with L >= need. bestRisk/bestSafe and the switch exactly as c1023-r2-24: risk-on if bestRisk exists and R(bestRisk) > 0 and (bestSafe absent or R(bestRisk) > R(bestSafe)). Risk-on: var = sample variance of ret(b_bestRisk, e-j), j = 0..volWindow-1, times 252; w = var > 0 ? min(1, targetVar/var) : 1 (c1023-r2-23's overlay, 20% vol target); weights {bestRisk: w, bestSafe: 1-w} (if bestSafe is absent the 1-w stays cash). Risk-off: {bestSafe: 1}; neither scored: ew. Monthly, long-only.
rationale: r2-23 tested the Moreira-Muir overlay on a 1.1pp base and failed a neighbour; r2-24's 7.1pp base is large enough to carry the overlay test, and scaling only the risk leg down into the safe pick is the natural place for it in a dual-momentum switcher.

name: 9-ETF dual momentum with the absolute-momentum hurdle set to SHY's 12-month return (textbook GEM), monthly
rule: Conventions: portfolio mode rank(universe,t,ctx); for symbol s, b = universe[s], L = b.length, e = L-1 (latest bar in the view = the rebalance-day close); ret(b,k) = b[k].close/b[k-1].close-1; crypto daily bars are contiguous so windows are aligned from the end; ties broken by symbol name ascending; weights >= 0 and sum <= 1, unlisted symbols = 0, {} = cash; ew = equal weight over every symbol in the view. R(s) = b[e].close/b[e-lookback].close-1 for a symbol in the view with L >= need (others unscored). bestRisk = scored risk symbol with the highest R (ties by name); bestBond = scored bond symbol with the highest R. hurdle = R(SHY) if SHY is scored, else 0. If bestRisk exists and R(bestRisk) > hurdle: return {bestRisk: 1} (no comparison with the bond leg: the textbook rule). Else if bestBond exists: return {bestBond: 1}. Else return ew. Monthly, long-only. Note stated now: in c1023-r2-24 SHY is inside the safe set, so 'beat the best safe asset' already implies 'beat SHY' and a hurdle swap alone would be a no-op; the textbook version therefore moves SHY out of the safe set and drops the risk-vs-bond relative test, which is the one structural difference from r2-24.
rationale: Antonacci's GEM measures absolute momentum against the T-bill return, not zero, so that in a rising-rate tape a risk asset must beat cash to be held; the discovery universe has SHY, and this is the widely used version people want answered.
source: campaign-1023/REPORT.md section 4 idea 17; extends c1023-r2-24 and c1022-acad-15/16/17 (SHY hurdle in other universes); Antonacci 2014 'Dual Momentum Investing'; Antonacci 2013 'Absolute Momentum'
